It will be a miracle if I can eat this well and still lose weight.
Feb 2015 • Solo
That is what I first thought when I received my first delivery meal in the 3.2.1. Slim plan from Nicole at Nutrifort and Good Eats. In this review I will reveal if a miracle has actually happened after being on the program for 2 weeks.

I have the good fortune of being a member of a Nutrifort gym in my apartment building and one day I noticed a poster for this plan they were running, whereby they deliver lunch and dinner and a couple of between meal snacks to me every weekday. The advert said that so long as I exercise 3 times a week, then I would lose weight.

Oddly, this was no more expensive than the meals I was having delivered anyway and certainly not much more than it would cost me in time, wasted ingredients, gas and taxi fares if I wanted to try and cook everything myself, so I thought I would give it a go.

The last diet I went on found me obsessing over buying and preparing low carb foods till late in the evening most nights of the week, since it required a lot of effort to make nice tasting recipes. I was delighted by the prospect that someone else could prepare everything for me and simply bring it to my door. 

 I was doubly delighted when the food turned up and it was a lot more tasty and plentiful than the usual plates full of cardboard and dirty dishwater or miniscule proportions that I have experienced with previous diets. 

It was at that point that I started thinking to myself that there was no way it was going to work. Especially since I cleaned my plate of every scrap of food – not because there was so little on the plate but because it was so tasty. Nicole had warned me that the portions were on the small side, but I found them perfectly adequate and filling. Plus, I knew that if I did feel hungry between meals I had the snack packs to rely on and I found that these were great for mid morning and mid afternoon – again tasty and imaginative snacks so it doesn’t get boring. On the subject of boring, the meals tend to be seasoned very delicately and as a lover of spicy food, I did find I needed to add a little spice of my own, but at the same time this means the restaurant is not throwing handfuls of salt in the food and for someone who is keeping an eye on his blood pressure, this is excellent news. 

So, the big question remains, after 2 weeks, did I lose any weight – YES! I lost just over half a kilo in 2 weeks. What’s more, this is a reasonably priced and sustainable diet, which takes zero effort on my part to undertake.

Highly recommended, I am an enthusiastic convert and I look forward to continuing on my journey to fitness and better health whilst eating tasty and filling meals at the same time.

As far as I can tell, this establishment's health claims are restricted to not seasoning their food properly and refusing to sell real coke! 

I had the meatball slider, with was under seasoned and came in a lightish bun made with at least 80 per cent refined white flour. As white flour is refined carbohydrate, I fail to see how this could be construed as 'healthy'.

The table salt was too damp and too large grained to add to my food at the table. HOWEVER, my fries, yes, deep-fried potato were covered in the stuff! Don't be fooled by about health claims, this lack of consistency comes down to the cooks not tasting the food. 

The oil the fries had been cooked in needed changing, as they came out rather dark. Old oil promotes the growth of Clostridium botulinum, especially in warm climates. Old, dark cooking oil is also packed with free radicals, which would have been mopped up by the tomato sauce in my slider, had I been given more than a teaspoon of the stuff.

I would also like to add that despite the menu claiming my fries were 'hand cut' and therefore implying they are made in site, they are not. They're frozen. 

In a reply made my management on this site to a previous customer's review, they say they don't serve unhealthy condiments. Rubbish. I was given a bowl of sugary ketchup to go with my salty fries! 

Like black pepper? Unlucky, as it wasn't on any of the table the day I visited

I was also taxed on my food, despite a sticker on the menu claiming otherwise.

Written June 2, 2014
nthankins
Thank you for your mail and rating. Please be advised of the following:
1) The bread bun for our meatball slider is homemade from a local baker made of wheat flour, with no preservatives. If you did not want refined carbohydrate, you might have opted to order it without the bun or a different item on the menu. Eating refined carbohydrate is not considered "unhealthy" unless it is saturated with sugar or preservatives!
2) Our table sea salt is kept in a container with large opening, and a hard shake usually does the trick. Black pepper was on a table next to you or a simple request from the wait staff would have taken care of that.
3) Our fries are hand cut then frozen in a container. We freeze them so when we cook them in hot oil for 3 min they can be crispy on the outside while soft on inside. We only serve 220g of fries on the side to keep the consumption of fried food limited. We serve ketchup on a separate side dish in case you want to dip the fries. 
4) The only items on the menu with VAT are specifically noted because they are often ordered to take away.
